messages: Carmen: Heads-up from an SR audit on Insights -> Table view. NVDA kept reading the column header twice after a sort change. Repro steps in ticket. Leo: thanks. which column and what does the DOM look like? Carmen: example snippet below — header is a th with role and we added a live region span to announce sort state: ``` Name sorted ascending ``` When you press Enter to sort, NVDA says "Name" then immediately reads "sorted ascending" then re-reads "Name". Feels like a duplicate/interruptive announcement. Priya: yeah that pattern can cause SR to re-announce the focused element when a descendant updates. The live update is inside the focused node. Marco: quick fix idea: move the live region outside the interactive header subtree so updating it doesn't retrigger reading of the header itself. Or use aria-sort on the th instead of a live region. Leo: agree on aria-sort; it's the semantic way to indicate sort state. e.g. `Name` SRs will announce sort without a live region. Carmen: tried changing to aria-sort locally and removing the inner live span — NVDA announced "Name column sorted ascending" once and no double read. Priya: nice. two extra nits: • prefer putting the interactive control as a native button inside the th rather than role=button on the th itself. that gives correct semantics and keyboard handling. • ensure focus outline is visible: the table uses thin focus ring in compact mode; when header gets focused it's hard to see on the gradient header row. Marco: for the button approach we'd have `` then manage aria-pressed or aria-sort on the th. Should we keep aria-sort on th and button just toggles? Leo: recommended pattern: th[aria-sort] with a button inside. Button has aria-label that includes context if needed. aria-sort is the source of truth and is updated by the click handler. Carmen: also noticed heading hierarchy weirdness in the panel: panel title is an h4 while page sections above are h2/h3 — VoiceOver users complained they couldn't find the table as heading levels jumped.
